chunks: Verily Qarun was of Moses' people, but he began to oppress them. We had given him treasures, so many that a team of wrestlers could hardly lift their keys. His people said to him: "Do not be exultant. God does not like those who exult."

key_terms.قَارُونَ: Qarun (Korah), a wealthy man contemporary to Prophet Moses

ai.seo_question: Who was Qarun in the Quran and what was his relationship with Prophet Moses?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, Qarun is often interpreted not merely as a wealthy individual but as a symbol of those who possess divine knowledge or blessings yet fail to recognize their Source, leading to spiritual arrogance. The advice of his people underscores the Shia emphasis on *zuhd* (asceticism) and the danger of worldly attachment (*hubb al-dunya*) corrupting the heart. This narrative serves as a cautionary tale against the misuse of material resources and the loss of humility before God.
